about: Framework-agnostic adapter conformance spec. Every adapter implements each case as a fixture in its framework and must classify it as stated. 'evidence' names the layer the adapter produces: source (ast-grep patterns), static-cases (the static test-case collector, checked as if every test function were new), run-report (guarded run plus normalised JUnit report) or collection (collect-only IDs per tier). 'expect' is finding (the rule reports it), clean (the rule does not), or a normalised record or collected IDs the adapter must produce.

cases.situation: a test patches a function of an owned package by its dotted name
a test patches an attribute of an imported owned module object
a test rebinds an attribute of an owned module by assignment
a test builds a mock specced on an owned class
a test fakes only an owned adapter interface that wraps a third party
a test carries a static skip marker with no approved exception
the same static skip is covered by a reason-backed guardrail exception for its path
a test is marked for automatic reruns until green
a test is marked as an expected failure
a property test neither fixes nor reports its seed
a property test fixes its seed
owned production code branches on a test-marker environment variable
owned production code declares a parameter that exists only for tests
owned production code reads only real configuration
a T1 test opens a network connection
a T1 test starts a process
a T1 fixture starts a process during teardown
a T1 test catches the guard's error and carries on
a T1 test computes in memory and writes only its temporary directory; the report shows the tier's guards
a test writes a file under the user's real home directory
a test writes under its temporary directory and the redirected home
a test skips at runtime; the normalised record keeps the outcome and reason for the shared report check
an expected failure is normalised as xfail with its reason
each test function has a descriptive behavior name; one name covers all parameter rows
a test function has only a generic single-word name
a test function's name holds only placeholder text
a tier selector collects no tests
a tier selector lists exactly the tests it selects
